context.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for low-bandwidth rural connections.

## Key Elements
- **Users:** Patients, Licensed Clinicians, Compliance & Audit Officers
- **Systems:** EU Telehealth System, US Telehealth System, Global Identity Provider (IdP)
- **External Services:** Third-Party National E-Prescription Gateways (EU), Pharmacy Networks (US), Video Relay/Codec Service, Clinician Accreditation Validator
- **Infrastructure:** Centralized Observability Plane, Global Traffic Management (Anycast DNS), Regional KMS

## Relationships
- **Patients & Clinicians** -> **EU/US Telehealth Systems**: HTTPS (Web/Mobile) and WebRTC for low-bandwidth video
- **EU/US Telehealth Systems** -> **Global IdP**: OIDC/OAuth 2.0 over HTTPS with MFA
- **EU/US Telehealth Systems** -> **National E-Prescription Gateways / US Pharmacy Networks**: mTLS REST / HL7 FHIR
- **Compliance & Audit Officers** -> **Regional Systems**: Restricted HTTPS for audit log access

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Provider:** Google Cloud Platform (GCP) deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`
- **Security & Encryption:** TLS 1.3, mTLS, Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) via regional KMS
- **Authentication:** OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect via Global IdP
- **Interoperability:** HL7 FHIR (US) and national standards (EU)
- **Networking & Resilience:** Envoy proxy sidecars for network shaping (sub-300 kbit/s degradation)

## Rationale
Sovereign regional boundaries (`europe-west3` and `us-central1`) strictly enforce GDPR and HIPAA data residency mandates without cross-region data replication. Decoupled container architectures and resilient video codecs guarantee continuous, low-bandwidth operational availability for rural users.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency and compliance via GCP.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU and US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Web/Mobile Frontend App (React/Flutter)
- API Gateway / Core Backend (Go/Node.js)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python/FastAPI)
- Interoperability Adapter (Plugin architecture)
- Video Session Manager (WebRTC SFU)
- External Systems (Global IdP, EU E-Prescription Gateways, US Pharmacy Networks, Video Relay)

## Relationships
- Clients to API Gateway via HTTPS/gRPC
- Interoperability Adapter to EU gateways and US pharmacies via REST/SOAP (HL7 FHIR / national standards)
- Video Session Manager to Web/Mobile Frontend via WebRTC
- Inter-container traffic secured via mTLS (SPIFFE/SPIRE on GKE)

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: Google Cloud Platform (`europe-west3` and `us-central1` regions)
- Encryption: GCP Cloud KMS (CMEK, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit)
- Security: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, GCP Cloud HSM for cryptographic AI output signing, GCP Secret Manager
- Observability: Prometheus/Grafana, Fluentbit sidecars streaming to GCP BigQuery

## Rationale
Regional container clusters on GCP strictly isolate EU and US health data to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA requirements. The microservices architecture with regional SFUs and pluggable interoperability adapters ensures high availability under unstable rural network conditions and rapid scaling across diverse healthcare jurisdictions.

Web/Mobile Frontend App.analysis:
## Overview
[A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients.]
[Ensures strict GDPR and HIPAA compliance with region-locked data residency and offline resilience for rural areas.]

## Key Elements
- Web/Mobile Frontend App (React / Flutter)
- Routing & Shell Component
- Consent & Privacy Manager Component
- AI Symptom Checker UI Component
- Video Streaming Interface Component
- API Client & Local Storage Adapter

## Relationships
- Routing & Shell Component -> Consent & Privacy Manager Component: Manages UI state [In-Memory]
- Consent & Privacy Manager Component -> API Client & Local Storage Adapter: Syncs consent states [HTTPS/REST]
- AI Symptom Checker UI Component -> API Client & Local Storage Adapter: Sends symptom payloads [HTTPS/gRPC]
- Video Streaming Interface Component -> Video Session Manager: Establishes media streams [WebRTC]
- API Client & Local Storage Adapter -> API Gateway / Core Backend: Sends API requests [HTTPS/gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- React / Flutter: Builds a responsive Progressive Web App and mobile interface supporting low-bandwidth conditions
- Firebase Hosting / Cloud Storage + Cloud CDN: Regional edge hosting enforcing data residency in europe-west3 and us-central1
- WebRTC SDKs: Enables video streaming with adaptive bitrate controls for connections under 300 kbit/s
- AES-GCM / Secure Hardware: Encrypts cached patient health data bound to device Keychain/Keystore

## Rationale
[This architecture ensures regional data segregation and strict compliance with EU GDPR and US HIPAA mandates.]
[Client-side caching and adaptive video streaming provide reliable healthcare delivery for rural users with unstable internet.]

API Gateway / Core Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. The system enforces strict regional data residency and compliance with GDPR and HIPAA.

## Key Elements
- Patients, Licensed Clinicians, Pharmacy Partners, Compliance & Audit Officers
- Global Identity Provider (IdP)
- Web/Mobile Frontend App (React / Flutter)
- API Gateway / Core Backend (Go / Node.js)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Adapter (Plugin architecture)
- Video Session Manager (WebRTC SFU)
- Regional Redis Cache, Regional Kubernetes (GKE) Clusters

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Frontend App -> API Gateway / Core Backend: Sends API requests via HTTPS / gRPC with protobuf compression
- API Gateway / Core Backend -> AI Symptom Checker: Requests AI symptom analysis via mTLS / Internal API
- API Gateway / Core Backend -> Interoperability Adapter: Triggers e-prescription routing via mTLS / Internal API
- API Gateway / Core Backend -> Global Identity Provider (IdP): Authenticates users via OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with DPoP

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for the API Gateway / Core Backend to ensure high throughput and low latency.
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` to enforce regional data residency.
- Regional Redis Cache: Used by the Idempotency & Retry Coordinator for safe transaction retries without cross-border leaks.
- OpenTelemetry: Implemented for distributed tracing with PHI/PII payload scrubbing.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional data isolation and consent management at the API gateway layer to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA requirements. Using lightweight protocols like gRPC and protobuf compression ensures high availability and resilience for rural patients on unstable connections.

AI Symptom Checker.analysis:
## Overview
- Secure, cross-border telemedicine platform offering video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US.
- Engineered to ensure strict regulatory compliance (GDPR, HIPAA, EU MDR) and high availability over unstable rural internet connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Licensed Clinicians
- Web/Mobile Frontend App (`React / Flutter`)
- API Gateway / Core Backend (`Go / Node.js`)
- AI Symptom Checker Container (`Python / FastAPI`), comprising:
  - Triage API Controller (`Python / FastAPI`)
  - Inference Engine (`Python / PyTorch` or `ONNX Runtime`)
  - Clinical Fallback Engine (`Python / Rule-based Logic`)
  - Audit & Cryptographic Signer (`Python / GCP KMS / Cloud HSM Client`)
- External Systems: Global IdP, EU National E-Prescription Gateways, US Pharmacy Networks, Video Relay/Codec Service (WebRTC SFU)

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Frontend App -> API Gateway / Core Backend: Manages sessions and requests triage [HTTPS / REST]
- API Gateway / Core Backend -> Triage API Controller: Requests AI symptom analysis [mTLS / Internal API]
- Triage API Controller -> Inference Engine: Executes clinical model [In-memory / gRPC]
- Triage API Controller -> Clinical Fallback Engine: Invokes fallback on model failure/timeout [In-memory]
- Triage API Controller -> Audit & Cryptographic Signer: Offloads event logs [Async Message Queue]
- Audit & Cryptographic Signer -> GCP Cloud HSM / KMS: Cryptographically signs audit payload [gRPC / Regional HSM Endpoint]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (`GCP`): Target cloud provider for global infrastructure.
- GKE Autopilot (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Regional container orchestration ensuring strict data residency isolation.
- GCP Cloud HSM / KMS: Cryptographically signs audit payloads and secures data at rest via CMEK.
- Python / FastAPI / PyTorch / ONNX Runtime: Powers high-performance, low-latency AI symptom checking and fallback logic.
- WebRTC SFU: Powers video consultations with degraded mode support for low-bandwidth connections.

## Rationale
- Regional GKE deployment with strict network policies ensures health data never crosses international boundaries, satisfying GDPR and HIPAA mandates.
- Asynchronous cryptographic signing and local fallback engines maintain sub-3-second latency and high availability for rural users while guaranteeing EU MDR traceability.

Interoperability Adapter.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability over unstable connections.

## Key Elements
- **Interoperability Adapter Container**: Manages cross-border prescription routing and external gateway communication.
- **EU Gateway Plugin**: Translates core payloads to national EU standards using Go.
- **US FHIR Translator**: Maps payloads to US HL7 FHIR resources using Go and HAPI FHIR Java.
- **Regional Routing Engine**: Enforces data residency by directing traffic to regional endpoints.
- **Delivery Status Notifier**: Asynchronously pushes delivery acknowledgements via GCP Pub/Sub.
- **Audit Ledger & Receipt Signer**: Signs payloads and receipts using Google Cloud KMS.
- **External Gateways**: EU E-Prescription Gateways and US Pharmacy Networks.

## Relationships
- API Gateway / Core Backend -> Interoperability Adapter: Triggers e-prescription routing via mTLS and Internal API.
- Regional Routing Engine -> EU Gateway Plugin / US FHIR Translator: Delegates payload transformation via in-memory communication or gRPC.
- EU Gateway Plugin / US FHIR Translator -> Audit Ledger & Receipt Signer: Requests cryptographic signatures via in-memory communication or gRPC.
- Delivery Status Notifier -> API Gateway / Core Backend: Publishes signed delivery receipts via GCP Pub/Sub.
- Interoperability Adapter -> EU E-Prescription Gateways: Transmits EU prescriptions using REST, SOAP, and HL7 FHIR over mTLS.
- Interoperability Adapter -> US Pharmacy Networks: Transmits US prescriptions using REST, SOAP, and HL7 FHIR over mTLS.

## Technology Stack
- **Go**: Core implementation language for high performance and low resource consumption.
- **GCP Pub/Sub**: Asynchronous messaging for reliable delivery status notifications under unstable network conditions.
- **Google Cloud KMS**: Region-specific key management for generating tamper-proof cryptographic audit receipts.
- **GCP Secret Manager**: Secure storage for external gateway mTLS private keys and certificates.
- **GCP Cloud Logging**: Centralized logging with PHI/PII masking enforced for GDPR and HIPAA compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces data residency by deploying isolated regional instances in europe-west3 and us-central1. Asynchronous queuing and cryptographic auditing ensure compliance, reliability, and non-repudiation for cross-border healthcare transactions.

Video Session Manager.analysis:
## Overview
The Video Session Manager coordinates real-time video consultations for a cross-border telehealth platform operating in the EU and US. It ensures reliable, secure, and compliant streaming for patients with unstable internet connections.

## Key Elements
- SFU Media Router (Mediasoup / C++ & Node.js)
- Session Signaling Controller (Go)
- Session Audit & Metadata Logger (Go)
- Session State Cache (Redis / GCP Memorystore)
- Web/Mobile Frontend App (React / Flutter)

## Relationships
- Web/Mobile Frontend App -> Session Signaling Controller: WebSocket signaling and authentication [WSS over TLS 1.3, JSON]
- Web/Mobile Frontend App -> SFU Media Router: Video/audio streaming and adaptive bitrate controls [WebRTC, UDP/SRTP, DTLS-SRTP]
- Session Signaling Controller -> Session State Cache: Ephemeral session and reconnection state management [TCP, Redis Protocol]
- SFU Media Router -> Session State Cache: Transport state verification for ICE restarts [TCP, Redis Protocol]
- Session Audit & Metadata Logger -> Regional GCP Databases: Telemetry and metadata persistence [TCP, SQL]

## Technology Stack
- Mediasoup & Node.js/C++: High-performance WebRTC packet forwarding with simulcast and adaptive bitrate support
- Go: Low-latency signaling control and audit logging
- GCP Memorystore (Redis): In-memory ephemeral session caching with automated 60-second TTL
- GCP Compute Engine: Dedicated media-plane instances with static public IPs for UDP port range 10000-20000

## Rationale
Decomposing the video manager into specialized components supports adaptive streaming and a 30-second reconnection window for rural users. Regional deployment in europe-west3 and us-central1 strictly enforces GDPR and HIPAA data residency requirements.
